title: Evil lies in the ruling part, not in matter
source_text: Εἶτα, ὡς ἔχων μέν τινα περὶ τῆς τῶν κακῶν γενέσεως εἰπεῖν ἀποῤῥητότερα σιωπῶν δ᾿ ἐκεῖνα καὶ τὰ πλήθεσιν ἁρμόζοντα λέγων, φησὶ τὸ ἐξαρκεῖν εἰρῆσθαι εἰς πλῆθος περὶ τῆς τῶν κακῶν γενέσεως ὡς ἐκ θεοῦ μὲν οὐκ ἔστι κακὰ, ὕλῃ δὲ πρόσκειται καὶ τοῖς θνητοῖς ἐμπολιτεύεται. ἀληθὲς μὲν οὖν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι κακὰ ἐκ θεοῦ· καὶ κατὰ τὸν Ἱερεμίαν γὰρ ἡμῶν σαφὲς ὅτι „ἐκ στόματος κυρίου οὐκ ἐξελεύσεται τὰ κακὰ καὶ τὸ ἀγαθόν“· τὸ δὲ τὴν ὕλην τοῖς θνητοῖς ἐμπολιτευομένην αἰτίαν εἶναι τῶν κακῶν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς οὐκ ἀληθές. τὸ γὰρ ἑκάστου ἡγεμονικὸν αἴτιον τῆς ὑποστάσης ἐν αὐτῷ κακίας ἐστὶν, ἥτις ἐστὶ τὸ κακόν· κακὰ δὲ καὶ αἱ ἀπ᾿ αὐτῆς πράξεις. καὶ ἄλλο οὐδὲν ὡς πρὸς ἀκριβῆ λόγον καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς ἐστι κακόν. ἀλλ᾿ οἶδα τὸν λόγον δεόμενον πολλῆς ἐξεργασίας καὶ κατασκευῆς, χάριτι θεοῦ, φωτίζοντος τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν, δυναμένων γενέσθαι τῷ κριθέντι ὑπὸ θεοῦ ἀξίῳ καὶ τῆς περὶ τὸν τόπον τοῦτον γνώσεως.
pass_a_gloss: Then, as having (ἔχων) some more secret things (ἀπορρητότερα) to say about the coming-to-be of evils but being silent (σιωπῶν) on those and saying the things fitting (ἁρμόζοντα) the multitudes (πλήθεσιν), he says it suffices to have been said to the multitude about the coming-to-be of evils that evils are not from God, but adhere to matter and dwell among mortals. True (ἀληθές) then that evils are not from God; for also according to our Jeremiah (Ἱερεμίαν) it is clear that 'from the mouth (στόματος) of the Lord (κυρίου) shall not come forth (ἐξελεύσεται) the evils and the good (τὸ ἀγαθόν)'; but that matter dwelling among mortals is cause (αἰτίαν) of evils is according to us not true. For the ruling part (ἡγεμονικόν) of each is cause (αἴτιον) of the vice (κακίας) subsisting (ὑποστάσης) in it, which is the evil (τὸ κακόν); and evils also [are] the actions (πράξεις) from it. And nothing else as regards exact reckoning (πρὸς ἀκριβῆ λόγον) according to us is evil. But I know the subject (λόγον) needing much working out (ἐξεργασίας) and establishment/proof (κατασκευῆς), [which] can come to be by grace (χάριτι) of God enlightening (φωτίζοντος) the ruling part, for the one judged (κριθέντι) by God worthy (ἀξίῳ) also of the knowledge (γνώσεως) about this topic (τόπον).
pass_b_english: Then, as though he had something more secret to say about the origin of evils but kept silent about it and said only what suits the multitude, he says that it is enough to say to the multitude about the origin of evils that “evils are not from God, but cling to matter and have their home among mortals.”

Now it is true that evils are not from God. For according to our Jeremiah too it is plain that “out of the mouth of the Lord will not come forth evil things and the good” (Lamentations 3:38). But it is not true, in our view, that matter, having its home among mortals, is the cause of evils. For the ruling part of each person is the cause of the vice that exists in it, and this vice is what is evil; and the actions that come from it are evils too. And in our view, speaking strictly, nothing else is evil.

But I know that this subject needs much working out and proof. These can come, by the grace of God who enlightens the ruling part, to the one whom God has judged worthy of the knowledge of this subject too.

choices.choice: Lamentations 3:38: archaic 'shall not come forth' -> 'will not come forth'; verse and LXX numbering checked
'But that matter ... is the cause of evils is not true in our view' reordered to 'But it is not true, in our view, that matter ... is the cause of evils'
note: recorded that Origen's paraphrase makes matter, not evils, the thing dwelling among mortals

Origen ascribes Lamentations to Jeremiah ('our Jeremiah'). Lamentations 3:38 in the Septuagint reads ἐκ στόματος ὑψίστου ('of the Most High'); Origen's text has κυρίου ('of the Lord'). The Septuagint wording, as Origen reads it, is a denial that evil and good alike come from God's mouth; the Hebrew (and English Bibles from it) has a question affirming that both evil and good come from the Most High. Translated as Origen reads it, without smoothing toward the Hebrew; the plural 'evil things' against the singular 'the good' is kept, and the word order is left as in the Greek so the line is not made to say more than it does. Chapter numbering for Lamentations is the same in the Septuagint and English Bibles. Origen's paraphrase here has matter (not evils) 'having its home among mortals'; kept as he words it. δυναμένων γενέσθαι (genitive plural) is taken loosely with 'working out and proof'.
